audit_findings.title: Noncash AFUDC may be counted as owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $18 million in 2025, equal to 15.8% of the $113.8 million anchor; $23 million in 2024 and $19 million in 2023
audit_findings.mechanism: Noncash equity AFUDC enters net income, while borrowed-funds AFUDC reduces interest expense; retaining either amount increases OE and every projected and terminal cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: AFUDC from equity funds, included in Other income, net, was $ 18 million in 2025, $ 23 million in 2024, and $ 19 million in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in the supplied OE is not demonstrated because the calculation trace is absent. The filed cash-flow statement removes equity AFUDC from operating cash flow, but that does not establish that the separate OE calculation removed it. The quantified potential error is large relative to the anchor and therefore reasonably capable of changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year from net income to OE, identify both equity and borrowed-funds AFUDC, and rerun all scenarios after removing any AFUDC retained in the numerator.

audit_findings.title: The D&A add-back may erase funded asset-removal obligations
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back depreciation that represents customer-funded removal costs without deducting actual or normalized removal spending inflates OE; the associated regulatory liability also reduces rate base.
audit_findings.evidence: A component of depreciation expense includes estimated asset retirement removal costs allowed in customer prices.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that removal-cost accruals are included in depreciation and that customer collections accumulated to a $1,245 million regulatory liability at year-end 2025 and $1,266 million at June 30, 2026. It does not disclose the annual depreciation component or non-ARO removal expenditures needed to measure an OE adjustment. Capital expenditures are stated to include removal costs, so double counting is also possible unless the OE construction is traced.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the depreciation-study removal accrual, annual non-ARO removal expenditures, ARO settlements, and maintenance-capex composition; then rerun OE with one—and only one—deduction for normalized removal consumption.

audit_findings.title: A substantial unaccrued wrongful-death claim sits ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $375 million asserted claim, equal to 31.9% of bear, 22.9% of base, and 20.6% of bull equity value; actual net exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured judgment, settlement, or defense cost would reduce future OE, cash, or the equity bridge before value is allocated to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The lawsuit seeks a total of $ 375 million related to their deaths and surviving family members’ claims.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim and its scale are demonstrated, but liability is not: the case is early, PGE denies liability, other defendants are named, and no reasonably possible loss range is estimable. The asserted amount is not a probability-weighted loss, yet its scale relative to scenario equity values prevents a not-material conclusion without insurance and allocation evidence.
audit_findings.action: Obtain policy limits, exclusions, deductibles, defense-cost provisions, allocation among defendants, regulatory-recovery analysis, and counsel's probability-weighted exposure; rerun the bridge for the uninsured expected loss and separately stress the plausible adverse range.

audit_findings.title: Portland Harbor remediation exposure is unrecorded and potentially material
audit_findings.magnitude: $20 million liability recorded in Q2 2026 and $42 million PHERA regulatory asset at June 30, 2026; remaining and high-end exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: PGE's unrecovered remediation, orphan-share, legal, and financing costs would reduce the equity bridge or future OE; PHERA recoveries offset only eligible amounts that survive insurance, prudency, and earnings-test limitations.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s liability related to the cost of remediating Portland Harbor could be material to PGE’s financial position.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing means the exposure is no longer wholly unrecorded: PGE accrued a $20 million low-end liability for a subset of project areas and deferred it through PHERA. That amount is about 1.2% of base equity value, but it is not the full exposure. Allocation percentages, other project-area costs, orphan shares, insurance, and the high end remain unresolved, and PGE states the final liability could be material. The site's $2.5–$5.5 billion estimate is not PGE's share and cannot be used as its valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the preliminary allocation report, project-area cost estimates, orphan-share methodology, insurance schedule, PHERA eligibility and recovery timing; rerun the bridge using PGE's recorded liability plus the estimated unrecoverable portion of the completed liability range.

audit_findings.title: Tax-credit benefits may belong partly to customers and expire before the terminal period
audit_findings.magnitude: $48 million of 2025 energy-related federal tax-credit benefit, equal to 42.2% of the $113.8 million anchor; shareholder-retained adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Tax credits reduce income-tax expense and can increase OE, but customer deferrals remove part of that benefit and PTC expirations through 2034 reduce explicit-period and terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The tax credit deferrals are established to provide the benefit back to customers over a period agreed upon with the OPUC.
audit_findings.explanation: Current tax-credit benefits are demonstrably present in earnings, and the filing states that related deferrals return benefits to customers. It also establishes that PTC generation expires at specified dates through 2034. The record does not identify how much of the $48 million is retained by shareholders or show an expiration schedule in the valuation. Because the gross benefit is large relative to the anchor and the model grows current OE into a terminal value, this is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $48 million benefit among PTCs, ITC amortization, transfer discounts, customer deferrals, and shareholder-retained amounts; model each credit's filed expiration through 2034 and rerun the terminal value without expired benefits unless replacement credits are supported.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset consumption may disappear from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $14 million in 2025, equal to 12.3% of the $113.8 million anchor; 2025 finance-lease ROU amortization and principal cash outflow were each $14 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A blanket D&A add-back reverses finance-lease ROU amortization, while principal payments classified as financing cash flow can escape both operating cash flow and capital expenditures, omitting recurring leased-asset consumption from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating leases reflect lease expense on a straight-line basis, while finance leases result in the separate presentation of interest expense on the lease liability and amortization expense of the ROU asset.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed accounting and cash-flow amounts demonstrate the potential mismatch, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation separately deducted lease principal, renewal economics, or equivalent maintenance capex. A recurring omission near 12% of the anchor is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value. The $290 million year-end finance-lease liability is context, not the appropriate automatic equity deduction.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease ROU amortization, principal payments, renewals, and maintenance-capex deductions for every OE year, including the Pelton/Round Butte financing arrangement; rerun OE with one normalized deduction for recurring leased-asset consumption and no blanket lease-liability deduction.
